question: Why Tibbett Allen left the Board in 1888 is unknown. He was elected for Jefferson District in 1887; the county court issued a rule against him on 3 September 1888 to show cause why he should not be removed for non-residence; he resigned and Frank Hume was appointed in his place on 2 October. The court never ruled, so there is no finding that he was non-resident, and nothing records where he lived. He was the last Black member until 1986. The Black press did not cover it: the Washington Bee carries nothing in any issue from August to December 1888, the Richmond Planet has one digitized issue in all of 1888 and it is silent, the People's Advocate had ceased by 1884, and the National Republican's digitized run ends in May 1888.
settles: The Alexandria County court order book for 1888 at the Library of Virginia, which would carry the rule and its disposition, and the Board's minute books at the Center for Local History, which the 1967 compilation (arlhist1967officials) was read from; neither is online. A residence for Allen in the 1880 census would settle where he lived.

question: The same sitting of the county court that issued the rule against Allen removed every previously appointed policeman except Robert Walker (alexandriagazette1888rule). Whether that was a political purge of Readjuster-era appointees, and whether the men removed were Black, is unknown; Judge D. M. Chichester's politics and the date he took the bench have not been established. A county court term disposes of all county business at once, so the two items sharing a sitting is weak evidence on its own.
settles: The 1888 court order book would name the men removed and who replaced them; the Alexandria Gazette for the following weeks would name the replacements and is searchable from here. Who elected Chichester to the bench, and when, is in the General Assembly's journals.

question: From 1931 the county's and the state's records name every candidate for the Board, about 400 losing candidacies through 2025, but none of the losers has been matched to a census record or a press description for race. The table holds the 1931 three, whom the county marked, and every run by the four Black members since 1987; the claim that no Black candidate ran 1932-1986 is one sentence each in Pratt (1995) and Bestebreurtje (2017), not a check of the list, and after 1987 nothing is claimed at all. A year with no ring is therefore not a finding that no Black candidate ran. Nor does the general-election list reach the nomination stage: a candidate who lost a Democratic primary never reached the ballot, and primaries are recorded only patchily by the county from 1950 (3 in the 1950s, 1 in the 1960s, none 1970-89, 6 in the 1990s, 3 in the 2000s) and fully by the state from 2007, while a caucus or convention nomination is not a public record at all (Sally, 26 September 2026).
settles: Race-match the losing candidates: for 1932-1950 the census on Ancestry (a listing with a second thing in agreement, as board_census.csv requires), for later years a candidate profile or election-week piece in the Sun, the Post, ARLnow or the Sun Gazette; a row per candidate found, and the searched negatives recorded

question: Race by magisterial district is published for 1870 only: Table III gives Jefferson 383 white to 873 colored, Arlington 517 to 857, Washington 275 to 280. The 1880, 1890, 1900, 1910, 1920 and 1930 tables give the districts by total alone, and the composition tables in those volumes stop at the county, so the argument that single-member districts returned Black members while the Black population was concentrated has a district-level race figure at the start of the period and none at the end. 1890 cannot be recovered at any price, its manuscript schedules having burned; 1880 and 1900-1930 would need a full-count extract, a source class this repository does not yet use. Of the feasible years 1910 or 1920 would say the most, since they would show Jefferson's Black share falling while the county's white population climbs; 1880 sits inside a stretch the county-level series already covers.
settles: Decide which years are worth the extract, then scope it: whether IPUMS full-count coverage reaches these years and how its sub-county geography maps onto Virginia magisterial districts, neither checked. For 1880 read census1880schedule first - the Jefferson Township population schedule reproduced in hjerpe2021 appendices 1-3, marked not yet consulted directly - which may answer that year without an extract. Closes when the figure is built, or when the years are ruled out and the write-up says so
